title: Rock walls in the dehesa
description: Dry-stone walls between the sparse holm and cork oaks of the dehesa are very common in the province of Cáceres, and also common in Salamanca and Badajoz. Rare in Huelva, and absent from Sevilla and the south-east of Ciudad Real.

title: Salamanca winter Gen 3
description: The province of Salamanca has almost only winter Generation 3 coverage: leafless trees, low sun, brown grass.

title: Penedès vineyards
description: Vineyards between mountain ranges to the north and south, like La Rioja, but with Catalan roadlines and a lot of Generation 4. The southern part (Garraf) has rock walls similar to Mallorca's. Area: the Penedès, west of Barcelona.

title: Ribera del Duero
description: Vineyards along the Duero river, between Valladolid and Soria (Peñafiel, Aranda de Duero). Lots of stone pines, and small dry hills nearby when it is not flat.

title: Ribera del Miño vineyards
description: Along the Miño on the Portuguese border (south of Pontevedra), vineyards grow right next to the houses, in villages with northern Portuguese-looking architecture. Rural vineyards exist too.

title: Flat stone pine forests
description: Flat forests made only of stone pines (Pinus pinea) are found in Doñana, between Huelva and Sevilla, and between Valladolid and Segovia. Around Albacete they are mixed with fruit trees and red soil; north-east of Barcelona they grow on forested hills with other pines.

title: Scots pine regions
description: Scots pines (Pinus sylvestris, red trunk) come in four main areas: the Pyrenees (dense, mountainous forests), Soria, the high roads of the Sierra de Madrid, and Cuenca north-west of València (drier). North-west of Segovia and north-east of Ávila they form flat forests.

title: Aleppo pine distribution
description: The Aleppo pine (Pinus halepensis) is the most common pine in eastern Spain: País Valencià, Catalunya, Murcia and the Balearic Islands. It is rare elsewhere.

title: Monterey pine plantations
description: Plantations of Monterey pine (Pinus radiata) are found in the Basque Country, mostly Gipuzkoa and Bizkaia. Near the Bizkaia coast they mix with eucalyptus.

title: Pinus pinaster
description: The province of Segovia has flat forests of maritime pines (Pinus pinaster, mediterranean variant), a very recognisable type of forest. Galicia have them in a recognizable landsape.

title: Spanish juniper
description: The Spanish juniper (Juniperus thurifera, sabina) is a chubby, isolated tree growing alone in dry fields. Found in Guadalajara, Soria, Teruel and Segovia.

title: León poplar plantations
description: Around León, poplar plantations in the distance, lots of corn and reddish soil.

title: Teruel poplars
description: Teruel is mountainous and very dry. There are no poplar plantations, but many poplars grow along the rivers. Coverage is often from autumn.

title: Vegas del Guadiana
description: Along the Guadiana in Extremadura (between Mérida and Badajoz), green irrigated fields of corn and fruit trees, some olive trees, palms, and rows of eucalyptus instead of poplars. It is the only part of Extremadura without dehesa.

title: Pear orchards around Lleida
description: Pear orchards are grown mostly around Lleida, on flat land.

title: Pink almond blossom
description: Almond trees are very common in the east, but only Granada and Lleida have winter coverage, so pink blossoming almonds (February/March) point to one of those. Lleida is flat; Granada has big snowy mountains to the south.

title: Hazelnut orchards in Tarragona
description: Hazelnut orchards are very common in Tarragona, mostly in the coastal part near Reus.

title: Pre-Pyrenean peñas
description: Isolated limestone crags (peñas) rising above greener land run from the north of Burgos (where they are most numerous), through La Rioja (Sierra del Toloño), Navarra (Lóquiz, Andia, Urbasa) and Huesca (Leire, Peña de Oroel, Mallos de Riglos, Guara) to Catalunya (Montsec, Oliana, Querol).

title: La Marina peñas
description: In the north of Alacant (La Marina), peñas such as Montgó and Benicadell rise above pine forests and fruit trees; it is greener than the similar crags of Murcia (Yecla, Jumilla, Sierra de Pila, Orihuela).

title: Albufera rice fields
description: Flat rice fields with palm trees south of València, with big mountains to the south and hills to the west and north-west. Some coverage (March 2019) shows the fields without water.

title: Empordà plain
description: The flat Empordà in Girona has many fruit trees, poplars, corn, stone pines and cypresses.

title: Doñana rice fields
description: Around Doñana the landscape is stone pines, palm trees and eucalyptus. The rice fields near Isla Mayor can look drier than those of the other marshes.

title: Grey marl slopes
description: Grey, eroded marl (marga) slopes are pre-Pyrenean: best seen in the Jacetania valley, Sobrarbe and Ribagorça, and in Osona, where they appear in almost every location. Araba and the Pamplona basin have the soil but it is rarely visible.

title: Arid riverside cliffs
description: Bare, arid cliffs facing green irrigated fields along a river: around Zaragoza and Madrid, and east of Valladolid, where they are less dry and can carry forests.

title: Moncayo
description: The Moncayo, a large isolated mountain, should be visible to the south-west from every location in southern Navarra and western Aragón.

title: Garraf and Montsià rock walls
description: The comarques of El Garraf and El Montsià in Catalunya have dry-stone walls very similar to those of Mallorca.

title: Elche date palms
description: Groves of date palms are very common around Elx/Elche and the Vega Baja.

title: Lleida spring 2013 coverage
description: Around Lleida there is a lot of March–June 2013 coverage with a short antenna that always has a light halo. Flat, with fruit trees and poppies. March 2010 Gen 3 is also a good clue here.

title: La Rioja and Navarra summer 2013
description: La Rioja and Navarra have summer 2013 coverage with a short antenna without halo. Navarra has the most rural roads covered, with an arid look; green locations with corn and fruit trees are along the Ebro, Aragón and Arga rivers.

title: Aragón rural long antenna
description: Aragón is the only region whose extensive 2012 long-antenna coverage was not overwritten, so almost all rural long-antenna locations are in Aragón. Most are arid.

title: Medium antenna
description: A Generation 3 antenna shorter than the long one, with the black car visible. Uncommon and only in the north: Navarra most, then the Basque Country, Cantabria, Asturias, Galicia and a little Teruel.

title: White-top antenna on the Huesca–Lleida border
description: Besides eastern Andalucía, the white-top antenna is found along the border between Huesca and Lleida.

title: Grey car without antenna
description: A grey Generation 3 car without antenna, very similar to the Asturian black car, only found in the north-west of the province of Zamora, around Puebla de Sanabria.

title: Winter Generation 4
description: Winter Generation 4 is mostly around Pamplona and Logroño, where it may be snowy, and around Madrid; some in Asturias. New 2024 winter coverage also exists in Alacant, Bizkaia, western Gipuzkoa and around Calatayud.

title: Guadalajara April Generation 4
description: Generation 4 coverage of Guadalajara taken in April, with a unique look.

title: Square-root smudge
description: A smudge shaped like a square-root sign on Generation 2 coverage, seen in the province of Burgos.

title: Stickerman smudge
description: The stickerman smudge on Generation 2 coverage is found in the province of Ávila, in Aragón, and in some Pyrenean valleys of Lleida.

title: Catalan direction signs
description: Direction signs in Catalunya use a different typeface and a more rectangular shape than in the rest of Spain.

title: Arrow-shaped signs in Balears and València
description: Arrow-shaped direction signs with names in a large font. Far more common in the Balearic Islands than in País Valencià.

title: French-style signs in Gipuzkoa
description: Gipuzkoa sometimes uses French-style direction signs; occasionally also found in the other two Basque provinces.

title: Blue signposts around Alacant
description: Alacant, Orihuela and Mutxamel paint their signposts blue.

title: La Manga signposts
description: La Manga (Murcia) has blue signposts, and blue posts with red and yellow bands.

title: Brown sign backs in Fuerteventura
description: Signs on Fuerteventura have brown backs and posts.

title: Generalitat sticker
description: The back of signs in Catalunya often carries the Generalitat logo sticker. Many signs have no sticker at all.

title: Diputació de Barcelona sticker
description: A Diputació de Barcelona sticker on the back of signs is exclusive to the province of Barcelona. Note the two horizontal mounting bars and the round signpost, typical of Catalunya, the Balearics and the Basque Country.

title: Navarra sticker
description: Signs in Navarra carry a C.F.N (Comunidad Foral de Navarra) or G.D.N sticker on the back.

title: Madrid sticker
description: Sign stickers in the Comunidad de Madrid show its flag (red with white stars).

title: Araba sticker
description: Signs in Araba carry a D.F.A/A.F.A sticker (Diputación Foral de Álava / Araba Foru Aldundia).

title: Gipuzkoa sticker
description: Signs in Gipuzkoa carry a G.F.A/D.F.G sticker (Gipuzkoa Foru Aldundia / Diputación Foral de Guipúzcoa).

title: Bizkaia sticker
description: Signs in Bizkaia carry a B.F.A/D.F.B sticker (Bizkaia Foru Aldundia / Diputación Foral de Bizkaia).

title: Galicia sticker
description: Sign stickers in Galicia have the shape of the region with a diagonal stripe imitating the flag.

title: Andalucía sticker
description: Sign stickers in Andalucía show the Junta de Andalucía logo and the flag.

title: Andalusian coat-of-arms bollard
description: A bollard with the Andalusian coat of arms, sometimes hard to spot. Only on some A-roads in Huelva and Sevilla.

title: Catalan close-set roadlines
description: Solid outer lines with dashed centre lines very close together. Also seen elsewhere, but the double guardrail is far more common in Catalunya than in the rest of Spain.

title: Catalan dashed outer lines
description: Dashed outer lines with a solid centre line: a Catalan roadline pattern.

title: White roadside drainage
description: A white concrete drainage channel at the roadside. Found in most of Spain, but most common in Catalunya.

title: Albacete roadlines
description: Like the Barcelona close-set roadlines but with dashes in the middle, on lighter asphalt.

title: Two-tone asphalt in Castilla y León
description: Darker asphalt between the lines and lighter asphalt outside them is common on the main roads of Castilla y León; also found on some N-roads elsewhere.

title: Gipuzkoa long dashed outer lines
description: Long dashed outer lines are unique to Gipuzkoa.

title: Araba rural roadlines
description: Rural roads in Araba have close-set dashed centre lines and no outer lines.

title: Aragón rural roads
description: Rural roads in Aragón are of poor quality with solid outer lines; Aragonese bollards and long-antenna coverage are common on them.

title: Pink asphalt
description: Extremadura and western Castilla-La Mancha have pinkish asphalt; Aragón sometimes too.

title: Curb colours at intersections
description: Each region paints intersection curbs in its own colours (author's map). Not very reliable, but useful to narrow down.

title: Galician galerías
description: Enclosed glazed balconies (galerías) are very common on buildings in Galicia.

title: Black tiled roofs
description: Black tiled roofs (not slate) are common in the province of Lugo, around Santiago de Compostela and A Coruña, and on the western Asturian coast near Navia and Ribadeo.

title: Colourful Asturian houses
description: Asturian houses are similar to Cantabrian ones but often painted in bright colours.

title: Cantabrian wooden balconies
description: This type of wooden balcony on stone houses is exclusive to Cantabria. Cantabrian houses are not colourful, have no black roofs, and are often built of yellowish stone.

title: Small roofs over doors
description: Small wood-and-red-tile roofs over doors are Cantabrian.

title: Santander sign
description: A unique sign found in the city of Santander.

title: Basque concrete guardrail
description: This low concrete guardrail is only found in the Basque Country, where it is very common.

title: Basque wooden fences
description: These wooden fences, picket or rail, are only found in the Basque Country.

title: Baztán pink stone
description: In the Baztán valley (northern Navarra), buildings use pink stone.

title: Ribera del Ebro brick
description: Southern Navarra and La Rioja (Ribera del Ebro) use lots of light brown brick, often with mudéjar style, like Aragón.

title: Aragonese brick towns
description: Towns in Aragón feature lots of brick and mudéjar-style buildings.

title: Aragón comarca signs
description: Town entrance signs in Aragón name the comarca at the top.

title: Castilian water towers
description: These brick water towers are unique to Castilla y León.

title: Palomares
description: Round dovecotes (palomares) in the fields are unique to Castilla y León.

title: Red brick around León
description: Towns around León and Benavente have plain houses of red brick and adobe, often looking empty.

title: Green benches in Burgos
description: Green metal benches are very common in the province of Burgos.

title: Catalan openwork walls
description: Low garden walls topped with openwork concrete blocks are typical of Catalan houses (designs vary).

title: Wall-mounted pole brackets
description: Metal brackets on house walls carrying the power lines, in place of poles, are very common in Catalunya.

title: Blue-tiled church domes
description: Churches in País Valencià and Murcia often have domes covered in blue glazed tiles; Albacete too, slightly different.

title: Vega Baja houses
description: Low single-storey houses like this are common in the Vega Baja (south of Alacant) and the Huerta de Murcia.

title: Balearic green shutters
description: Houses in the Balearic Islands have characteristic louvred shutters, usually green.

title: Mallorcan beige stone
description: Houses in Mallorca tend to be built of beige stone.

title: Menorcan pastel houses
description: Houses in Menorca tend to be white or painted in pastel colours.

title: Menorcan white-topped walls
description: Dry-stone walls with white paint on top point to Menorca.

title: Ibiza white and yellow houses
description: Outside the old town, Ibiza has shabbier architecture; white houses with yellow corners are common.

title: Sevilla and Huelva houses
description: White houses with ochre or yellow trim around windows and doors are typical of Sevilla and Huelva.

title: Cádiz and Jerez houses
description: Cádiz and Jerez have tall white houses with yellow trim and large window grilles.

title: Lanzarote and Fuerteventura houses
description: Houses on Lanzarote and Fuerteventura are very white with shutters. Lanzarote is darker and greener; Fuerteventura is very arid.

title: Tenerife wooden balconies
description: Traditional houses on Tenerife have elaborate dark wooden balconies.

title: Perforated metal poles in Murcia
description: Metal poles with rows of holes are common in Murcia (little research, may exist elsewhere).

title: Catalan poletops with insulators
description: Poletops with insulators, on round metal or wooden poles, are distinctive of Catalunya; also common in the Balearics and sometimes in Aragón. Elsewhere in Spain they are rare.

title: Green pylons in Bizkaia
description: Lattice pylons found all over Spain are painted green in Bizkaia and its surroundings (spilling into Araba, Gipuzkoa and Cantabria).

title: Round concrete poles near Zaragoza
description: Round concrete poles, Argentinian-style, are very common around Zaragoza and up the Ebro (Tudela, Alfaro, Calahorra).

title: Madrid sidewalk
description: This sidewalk is very common in Madrid and is its strongest clue.

title: Madrid triangle fence
description: This metal fence with triangular bracing is very typical of Madrid.

title: Barcelona panot
description: The flower-patterned panot tile is found in Barcelona and its surroundings.

title: Bilbao flower tiles
description: A tile similar to the Barcelona panot, found in Bilbao and its surroundings.

title: Garraf sidewalk
description: This circle-patterned sidewalk is from the Garraf (around Vilanova i la Geltrú).

title: Donostia hexagonal sidewalk
description: Blue and white hexagonal tiles are the sidewalk of Donostia/San Sebastián.

title: Sevilla hexagonal sidewalk
description: Sevilla also has a hexagonal sidewalk, but grey.

title: Northern Navarra stone pavement
description: Pavements of irregular, usually reddish stones come from northern Navarra.

title: Navarra concrete streets
description: Streets in Navarran towns are often made of concrete. 90% of the time it is Navarra; otherwise La Rioja or Aragón near the border.
